Api.description: Storage API name, e.g. GetObject (OpenDAL ServiceOperation)

oneOf.description: Evenly spaced: one arrival every `1 / rate` seconds.

A Poisson process: exponentially distributed gaps with mean `1 / rate` (bursty, like
independent clients).

Bottleneck.description: The layer that dominates operation latency.

oneOf.description: Waiting for in-flight request permits / pooled connections.
Client-side processing (CPU, OpenDAL, response consumption).
DNS / TCP / TLS / proxy handshakes.
Uploading request bodies.
Server time to first byte.
Downloading response bodies.
Rate limiting (429/503).
Sleeping between retry attempts (errors that are not throttling).
In-process backend (memory/fs) service time.

ByteSize.description: A byte size: `4MiB`, `512KiB`, `1GB` (a plain number of bytes is accepted on input).

backend_down_bytes.description: Response body bytes downloaded from the backend.

backend_up_bytes.description: Request body bytes uploaded to the backend.

cache_hit_bytes.description: Logical read bytes answered by the local cache.

logical_read_bytes.description: Bytes the application asked to read.

overread_ratio.description: backend_down / (logical_read - cache_hit_bytes): over-fetch from range coalescing & chunking.

read_amplification_ratio.description: backend_down / logical_read (cache hits lower it, over-fetching raises it).

wire_rx_bytes.description: Raw socket bytes incl. TLS records and HTTP headers.

Cache.description:
`FoyerLayer` over an in-memory foyer cache of `memory` bytes of data: any object no larger
than `memory` is cached whole, a larger one is read through.

Capacity.description: How much load the target takes (design v4 §3); `report.capacity`.

calibration_bias_ratio.description:
Measured / predicted throughput of earlier verifications of this target and workload
([`calibrate`]); [`Capacity::predict`] scales its throughput by it.

confidence_reason.description: Why the confidence is what it is.

hypotheses.description: Competing limit models, the selected one first (design v5 §4).

inflight_ceiling.description:
In-flight requests the server accepts before it throttles (none: no throttling seen,
or throttling unrelated to concurrency).

rate_ceiling_requests_per_s.description:
The fitted rate limit (requests per second) when the selected hypothesis is a rate
limit (the lowest rate of a time-varying one); never the observed throughput.

CapacitySource.description: Where a capacity estimate comes from.

oneOf.description: Estimated from this run's rows.
From a tuner search.
Loaded from `<data>/capacity.toml` (an earlier run of the same target and workload).

Ceiling.description: The in-flight level the service accepts before it throttles.

hi_inflight_count.description:
First level clearly throttled above every plausible split, plus one level of
measurement error (the limit is in `[lo, hi)`).

inflight_count.description:
In-flight requests the service accepts: the estimate (the likeliest split);
`lo ≤ inflight_count < hi`.

lo_inflight_count.description:
Lowest level the limit may lie at: the lowest split about as likely as the best, less
one level of client-side measurement error.

verified.description: Re-listed after deletion and found nothing left.

cpu_pct.description: Process CPU usage in percent of ONE core (e.g. 350% = 3.5 cores busy).

ColdStartStats.description:
The cold start of a run: the connections dialed at the start of warmup and the operations
that waited for them.

connect.description: DNS + TCP + proxy + TLS of a fresh connection.

first_ops.description: Latency of the operations whose requests dialed.

Confidence.description: How far to trust the estimate.

cold_start.description:
Connection setup before warmup absorbed it (design v5 §3, M15): the dials and first
operations of the warmup's cold start.

existing_prefix.description: Benchmark **existing** objects under this prefix (read-only; nothing is written).

partitions.description: Spread objects across this many `part=NN/` prefixes.

persist.description:
Keep the generated dataset between runs (`oprobe-dataset/<fingerprint>/`) to avoid
re-uploading it every time (remove it with your storage tools).

size_dist.description: Object sizes drawn from a distribution (`object_size` is then its median).

DimensionSlice.description: One slice of a dimension (a prefix, a size bucket, cold or warm, a tenant).

throttled_ratio.description: Share of this slice's own requests that were throttled.

Dimensions.description: Where the traffic and the trouble are (`report.dimensions`, design v5 §3).

cold_warm.description: `cold` (first read of a key) and `warm` (repeat reads).

workers.description: Per-worker slices of a distributed run.

Direction.description: The direction of the bodies a [`HypothesisKind::BandwidthCap`] was fitted on.

oneOf.description: Response bodies (`bytes_down` over the body stage).
Request bodies (`bytes_up` over the send stage): an uplink at its capacity.

EffectiveKnobs.description: Knob values as OpenDAL applies them, which can differ from what was requested.

write_chunk_bytes.description:
Chunk (multipart part size) OpenDAL writes with: the requested chunk clamped to the
service's `write_multi_min_size ..= write_multi_max_size` (reads use it unchanged).

EnvInfo.description: Cloud context of the target, when known.

ErrorBody.description: Machine form of an error (`{"type":"error","error":{…}}` in json/ndjson output).

detail.description:
The whole error chain as the storage library reported it, when `message` leads with
the provider's error code or states the cause plainly instead (machine output only).

ErrorCode.description: Stable error code. Serialized as its dotted string (e.g. `net.timeout`).

Evidence.description: The numbers and trace references behind a finding.

text.description: The evidence in words, with numbers.

windows.description: Time windows (seconds from the window start) where it shows.

Finding.description:
A finding (design v6 §3 "Explain"): a cause, the evidence (the requests themselves) and
**one** OpenDAL remedy. No sizing numbers: a single run varies no load (T1, T2); `oprobe
prove` sizes the remedy.

confidence.description:
How sure the cause is: `high` only when the limit model explains most of the effect
and agrees across the run's halves (T8).

Heatmap.description:
Operation latency over time: `counts[t][l]` operations started in time bucket `t` whose
latency falls in latency bucket `l` (from the trace rows; sampled when the run is).

latency_buckets_ms.description: Lower bound of each latency bucket (log scale; the last bucket is open-ended).

t_buckets_s.description: Start of each time bucket, seconds from the window start.

hostname_hash.description: FNV-1a hash of the host name (identifies the machine without naming it).

HotKey.description: A hot key: its share of the traffic and of the throttling.

throttle_share_ratio.description:
Share of **all** throttled responses that went to this key (not the share of the key's
own requests: compare `DimensionSlice::throttled_ratio`).

ca_cert.description: An extra PEM CA bundle to trust.

insecure.description: Skip TLS certificate verification (self-signed development endpoints only).

proxy.description: Egress proxy URL; `none` ignores HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY (unset: the environment).

oneOf.description: Negotiate via ALPN (h2 preferred for https), HTTP/1.1 for plain http.
Force HTTP/1.1.
Require HTTP/2 (ALPN for https, prior knowledge for plain http).

HumanDuration.description: A duration: `10s`, `500ms`, `2m` (plain seconds are accepted on input).

bic.description: Bayesian information criterion `−2·LL + k·ln n` (lower is better; selection score).

evidence.description: Why the model fits, in words.

explains_ratio.description: Share of the throttled (or slowed) requests the model explains.

log_likelihood.description: Log-likelihood of the data under the model (absent until fitted).

HypothesisKind.description: The kind of limit a hypothesis asserts.

oneOf.description: The service accepts a number of requests in flight (`ceiling`).
A token bucket: requests per second (`rps`, `burst`).
A per-key or per-prefix rate (`key`, `rps`).
Latency grows with in-flight requests (`service_ms`, `servers`).
Aggregate bytes per second flat across streams (`bytes_per_s`).
The client itself is saturated (CPU, scheduling lag).
The limit changes over the run (change points).
No limit was reached.

HypothesisParams.description: The parameters of a limit model (the ones its kind uses are set).

change_points_s.description: Seconds into the window where a [`HypothesisKind::TimeVarying`] limit changed.

key.description: The key or prefix of a [`HypothesisKind::KeyLimit`] (the hottest one).

key_share_ratio.description: Share of the requests that went to `key`.

segment_requests_per_s.description: The rate of each segment between change points (requests per second).

inflight_count.description: Requests in flight when a request arrived (itself included).

LatencyHistogram.description:
The run's whole operation latency distribution as a log-scale histogram with
[`LatencyHistogram::BINS_PER_DECADE`] bins per decade (each bin ≈ 12 % wide): every
operation of the window, never sampled. Only non-empty bins are listed, ascending.

bins_per_decade_count.description: Bins per decade of the log scale.

lower_ms.description: Lower bound of each non-empty bin (ms).

upper_ms.description: Upper bound of each non-empty bin (ms, exclusive).

Layers.description: The layer stack: each key is one OpenDAL layer.

cache.description: `FoyerLayer` with an in-memory cache (off by default).

MixEntry.description: One weighted operation of the mix.

size_bytes.description: Read range / write size (absent: whole object).

suffix.description: `parquet_scan`: footer read with a suffix range, no HEAD.

Network.description: Network view: TLS, TCP and the remote addresses requests went to.

inflight_mean.description: Time-weighted mean of requests in flight.

levels.description: Arrivals per in-flight level (the evidence of the ceiling).

max_clean_inflight_count.description: Highest level a request arrived at and was served cleanly.

min_throttled_inflight_count.description: Lowest level a request arrived at and was throttled.

ops_inflight_mean.description: Operations in flight on average (≈ the workers of a closed-loop run).

ops_service_inflight_mean.description:
Operations in flight on average, retry backoff left out: the time operations were
served, which throughput scales with (backoff is waiting, not work; A3).

OpBreakdown.description:
Where the wall-clock time of a logical operation went (mean ms per op).
`queue + cache + backend + retry + client == latency mean` (exact for each op; see docs/metrics.md).

backend_ms.description: At least one backend request on the network (connect, send, TTFB, transfer).

client_ms.description: Everything else: OpenDAL processing, signing, buffering, CRC, response consumption.

queue_ms.description: Waiting for in-flight request permits / connections, with nothing on the wire.

retry_ms.description:
Retry backoff: the retry layer sleeping between a failed attempt and the next one
(with no request of the operation on the network or queued meanwhile).

inflight_per_op_mean.description: Requests one operation keeps in flight on average over its lifetime.

ops_count.description: Operations the shape was measured over.

peak_inflight_per_op_count.description:
The most requests one operation had in flight at once (the maximum over operations:
on a busy client the parallel reads of an op often fail to overlap, and a p95 then
under-counts the burst the server sees).

requests_per_op_mean.description: Backend requests per operation (mean, retries included).

sequential_ratio.description: Share of operation time with exactly one request in flight (1 = strictly sequential).

OpSpec.description: One weighted operation in the workload mix.

oneOf.description: Read a random range of `size` bytes, or the whole object when `size` is omitted.

`stat` + footer read + `columns` random column chunks fetched as one vectored read.
With `suffix`, the footer is read with a suffix range (`bytes=-N`) and no `stat`: one
request fewer per file.
Single PUT of `size` bytes.
Streaming multipart write of `size` bytes (chunked by `knobs.chunk_size`).
HEAD a dataset object.
LIST one dataset partition.
LIST one dataset partition `limit` keys per page (each page is a billed request).

Delete up to `batch` objects the workload wrote, in one batch (OpenDAL `Deleter`:
`DeleteObjects` where the service batches).
Server-side copy of a dataset object to a scratch key.
GET a dataset object through a presigned URL.

Optimistic-concurrency write of `size` bytes: create with `If-None-Match: *`, then
overwrite with `If-Match: <etag of the previous write>`.
Small write carrying `entries` user-metadata pairs and a content type.

censored_count.description:
Missed arrivals counted in the latency distribution as censored values (a lower bound:
window end − intended start): `summary.latency` percentiles are then "≥" values.

intended_count.description: Arrivals due inside the window: started plus missed.

missed_count.description:
Arrivals that never started: still queued behind `concurrency` busy slots when the
window ended, or dropped after falling more than `knobs.timeout` behind schedule.
Arrivals that waited for a slot and then ran are not missed: their queueing delay is
part of their latency (measured from the intended start).

schedule.description: The `schedule` stage: intended → actual start of the operations that started.

OperatorSpec.description: One OpenDAL operator: service, layers, read/write options, HTTP client settings.

options.description:
OpenDAL service options (checked against the service). Values may reference
environment variables as `${NAME}`.

url.description:
The service: any OpenDAL scheme oprobe is built with (`s3://bucket/prefix`,
`gcs://bucket`, `fs:///tmp/x`, `memory://`), or `lab://SCENARIO` for the local lab.

measured_s.description: Seconds of the measurement window that ran.

PartialReason.description: Why a run stopped before its configured end.

oneOf.description: Ctrl-C, Stop or a cancelled job.
A safety budget (`--max-requests`, `--max-bytes`, `--max-duration`, `--max-cost-usd`).
A fatal error ended the measurement.

Preset.description: The workload presets: OpenDAL access patterns (design v6 §8).

oneOf.description: Many small objects: whole-object reads and writes, some stats.
Large objects: multipart writes and full reads.
Range reads (parquet-like): a stat, the footer, then vectored column-chunk ranges.
Metadata: list and stat over a partitioned prefix.

Profile.description: Complete, round-trippable profile of a run: the operator, the workload and the SLA.

RateShape.description: Time-varying open-loop rate: ramp:FROM..TO/DURATION, step:R1,R2,…/DURATION or diurnal[:MIN..MAX/PERIOD]

Remedy.description: The one remedy of a finding: an `OperatorSpec` path (design v6 §8 "Findings → remedies").

next.description:
The next command (`oprobe prove RUN CODE`, or `oprobe show RUN --by …` when there is
nothing to prove).

path.description:
The operator path the remedy changes (`layers.concurrent_limit.http`, `read.gap`);
absent when the remedy is not a layer (`key_limit`, `client_bound`, `errors`).

sized.description: `oprobe prove` sizes the value with a bracket search (otherwise it switches it on).

text.description: The remedy in one sentence (no numbers).

remote.description: `ip:port`, or `no connection` for the requests that failed without one (resets).

Report.description: The full report of one run.

capacity.description: How much load the target takes: the in-flight ceiling and the per-op request shape.

dimensions.description: Where the traffic and the trouble are: prefixes, hot keys, sizes, cold/warm, tenants.

effective_write.description:
The multipart part size OpenDAL wrote with (the requested `write.chunk` clamped to the
service's part-size limits).

latency_histogram.description:
Every operation's latency as a fine log-scale histogram (20 bins per decade, never
sampled): what the latency CDF is drawn from. Absent in reports before 6.3.

sampling.description: How the trace rows were sampled (findings use aggregate counts, never these).

schedule.description: Arrival schedule: missed arrivals and the schedule stage (design v5 §3).

self.description: The observer's own cost and the client's health (design v5 §3; `report.self`).

slowest.description: Op ids of the slowest operations (slowest first); their rows are in the run file.

spec.description: The replayable definition of the run (what `oprobe prove` replays).

timeline.description:
Per interval: 1 s for the first ten minutes, then 10 s. Operation counts and quantiles
by operation start; requests, throttled responses, retries and failures by when they
happened (see [`TimelinePoint`]).

retry_linking.description:
Whether the attempts of a retried call were linked into one operation (9.4). Absent
when it is not known: oprobe's own runs, and files written before 9.4.

tail_cuts_count.description: Requests actively cut by `TailCutLayer` to re-issue a faster attempt.

Retry.description: `RetryLayer` (OpenDAL's defaults: 3 times, 1 s to 60 s, factor 2, no jitter).

oneOf.description: Not known (not serialized).

A `RetryNotify` was installed: the attempts of a retried call are one operation, and
`retries_count` counts the retries.

An embedded layer without `Handle::retry_notify()`: each attempt is an operation of
its own (a retried failure is a failed operation), and `retries_count` stays 0
whatever was retried.

RunInfo.description: Identity and context of the run.

parent_id.description: The `oprobe prove` this run is a trial of (trials are hidden from `show --list`).

partial.description:
Why and when the run stopped early (absent for a complete run). A partial run is never
accepted as a baseline.

sampled.description: Trace rows were sampled (more requests than `trace.max_requests`); aggregates are exact.

source.description:
Where the traffic came from: a workload oprobe drove (`run`), or a production trace
an embedded `oprobe-trace` layer recorded (`trace`: no workload, nothing to replay).

RunSource.description: Where a run's traffic came from.

oneOf.description: A workload `oprobe run` drove (replayable: `oprobe prove` can A/B it).

A production trace written by the `oprobe-trace` layer (`oprobe.trace/9`): the
application's own traffic, with no workload to replay.

RunSpec.description: One replayable definition of a run.

operator_ref.description: The operator as given: a URL, an operator file or a configured name.

profile.description:
The fully resolved profile (preset defaults are kept implicit). Secret options of the
operator are `"<redacted>"` (environment references such as `${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}`
are kept: they are not secrets).

seed.description: The dataset / key-choice seed the run used.

Sampling.description:
How the trace rows were sampled (`report.sampling`, design v5 §2): whole operations are
kept with all their requests; findings use aggregate counts, never these.

always_kept_ops_count.description:
Operations kept regardless of the reservoir: the slowest 1 % and every failed or
throttled operation.

kept_ratio.description: Kept / seen operations (1 when nothing was sampled away).

ScheduleStats.description:
The arrival schedule (`report.schedule`, design v5 §3): open-loop arrivals that started
late or never, and the `schedule` stage (intended → actual start).

missed_arrivals_count.description: Arrivals that never started (censored latencies, counted in the tail as "≥").

open_loop.description:
Arrivals follow a rate (`--rate`, `--shape`, `--replay`); false: closed loop, subject to
coordinated omission.

schedule_stage.description: Time from an operation's intended start to its actual start.

SelfStats.description: The observer's own cost and the client's health (`report.self`, design v5 §3).

client_saturated.description: Lag p99 > 5 ms or CPU ≥ 90 % of the cores in use: the server/TTFB stage is unreliable.

cpu_ratio.description: Client CPU after warmup, as a share of the cores in use.

process.description: Process CPU and memory of the client (4.x `report.client`).

sched_lag_p99_ms.description: p99 of the 1 ms scheduling-lag probe.

SizeDist.description: Object size distribution: dist:lognormal(MEDIAN,SIGMA) or file:PATH

Sla.description:
Service level objectives. `oprobe run` / `oprobe tune` exit with code 3 when the measured
result breaches them (unless `enforce = false` / `--sla none`); the tuner rejects trials that
breach them and the diagnosis grades findings against them.

enforce.description: Turn a breach into exit code 3. Corrupted data (CRC mismatch) is always a breach.

max_throttle_rate.description:
Max fraction of operations that hit a 429/503 throttle. Unset: throttling that retries
absorb does not breach the SLA of a run (it is still a finding), and the tuner treats
any throttling as infeasible.

SlaInfo.description: Service level objectives the run was checked against.

max_throttled_request_ratio.description: Throttled responses / requests the run may have (`sla.max_throttle_rate`).

SlaVerdict.description: Outcome of checking a run against its [`Sla`].

breaches.description: One line per breached objective (empty when passed).

enforced.description: Whether a breach fails the command (exit code 3).

StageStats.description: Request stage distribution for one API (ms).

connect.description: DNS+TCP+proxy+TLS; only requests that dialed are counted.

request_p99.description: p99 of each request stage across every request (from the trace rows).

shares.description: Share of total operation time per layer (sums to ~100).

attempted_ops_per_s.description: Operations per second, failed ones included.

ops_per_s.description: Successful operations per second (goodput; failed operations are not throughput).

throttled_op_ratio.description: Operations with at least one throttled response / operations.

throttled_request_ratio.description: Throttled responses (429/503) / requests: what the SLA's throttle limit checks.

TailCut.description:
`TailCutLayer`: cancel (and, through `RetryLayer`, re-issue) a request slower than the
`percentile` of the recent latencies × `safety_factor`, the deadline clamped to
`[min_deadline, max_deadline]`.

The defaults are what oprobe measures with, not OpenDAL's (1.3, 200 samples, 500 ms, 30 s):
a shorter warm-up and floor so that short runs can see the layer work, and a ceiling at the
timeout that severs the same calls. Generated Rust spells out every value that differs from OpenDAL's default.

max_deadline.description:
The longest deadline (unset: the shorter of `layers.timeout.op` and `layers.timeout.io`,
the timeouts that sever the calls this layer times; 60 s without the timeout layer).

min_samples.description: Latencies recorded before the layer cuts anything.

percentile.description: The latency percentile the deadline follows (50..99).

window.description: The sliding window of latencies (at most 120 s).

name.description: Configured target name, when the run used one.

kernel.description: Kernel TCP statistics at request end (Linux `TCP_INFO`, macOS `TCP_CONNECTION_INFO`).

TcpKernelStats.description: Kernel TCP statistics (`TCP_INFO`) over the requests of the window.

retrans_count.description: Segments retransmitted, summed over connections (their last sample).

retransmitting_connections_count.description: Connections that retransmitted at least once.

rwnd_limited_ratio.description: Share of the busy (sending) time limited by the receive window / send buffer.

Throttle.description: `ThrottleLayer` (bytes per second, and the largest burst).

TimelinePoint.description:
One interval of the measurement window.

**When things count.** Operation counts (`ops_*`, `ok_ops_count`, `throttled_ops_count`),
bytes, the latency quantiles and `latency_rows_count` belong to the interval the operation
**started** in (they describe the same operations). Events count in the interval they
**happened** in: a request when it was sent (`requests_count`), a throttled response when
it arrived (`throttled_count`), a retry when it was issued (`retries_count`) and a failure
when the operation ended (`errors_count`) — a 503 at +7 s is drawn at +7 s, not at the
second its operation began.

cpu_pct.description: Client CPU in percent of one core (350 = 3.5 cores busy), when sampled in the interval.

errors_count.description: Operations that failed in the interval (counted when they ended).

goodput_ops_per_s.description:
Goodput: successful operations started in the interval per second (failed operations
never count; `ops_per_s` is the attempted rate).

inflight_peak_count.description: Peak requests in flight during the interval.

latency_rows_count.description:
Operations started in the interval per latency row of the heatmap
(`heatmap.latency_buckets_ms`): the heatmap is built from these, not from sampled rows.

len_s.description: Length of the interval: 1 s for the first ten minutes, 10 s afterwards.

missed_arrivals_count.description: Open-loop arrivals due in this interval that never started.

ok_ops_count.description: Operations started in the interval that succeeded.

ops_count.description: Operations started in the interval (the sample count behind its quantiles).

ops_per_s.description:
Operations started in the interval per second, failed ones included (the attempted
rate; `goodput_ops_per_s` counts successes only).

requests_count.description: Backend requests sent in the interval: every attempt, retries included.

retries_count.description: Retries issued in the interval (when the retry layer sent the next attempt).

t_s.description:
Start of the interval, seconds from the measurement window start (the same convention
as `heatmap.t_buckets_s`).

throttled_count.description:
Throttled responses (429/503) received in the interval, retries included (counted when
each response arrived). Before 6.3 this counted throttled operations by their start.

throttled_ops_count.description: Operations started in the interval that saw at least one throttled response.

verbs.description: The interval's counters per verb (`read`, `stat`, …), so a view can filter by verb.

Timeout.description: `TimeoutLayer` (OpenDAL's defaults: 60 s per operation, 10 s per I/O).

TlsHandshakeStats.description: TLS handshakes of the window (one per dialed connection).

hrr_count.description:
Handshakes that needed a HelloRetryRequest (an extra round trip: the client's first key
share was not one the server accepts).

handshakes.description: Full / resumed / HelloRetryRequest handshakes, versions, ciphers and groups.

TraceInfo.description: What the run file's trace rows cover.

sample_ratio.description: Kept / seen request rows (1 when nothing was sampled away).

oneOf.description: A sizing trial of the bracket search (the change at `value`).
The current operator (A).
The changed operator (B).

latency_rows_count.description:
Operations started in the interval per heatmap latency row (as
`TimelinePoint::latency_rows_count`): quantiles at row resolution.

latency_sum_ms.description: Sum of the latencies of the operations started in the interval (mean = sum ÷ ops).

throttled_count.description: Throttled responses received in the interval by this verb's operations.

exit_code.description:
What `oprobe run` exits with for this result (0, 3 SLA breach, 130 interrupted; 4/5 when
a safety rail stopped it).

headline.description: One sentence: where the time went.

oneOf.description: Worth a look (informational findings, warnings, partial run).
Warning findings.
Critical findings or a breached SLA.

arrivals.description: Open-loop arrival process: `constant` (evenly spaced) or `poisson` (design v5 §3).

cleanup.description: Delete everything written under the run prefix when the run ends.

concurrency.description: Concurrent logical operations (closed-loop workers, or the open-loop in-flight cap).

dataset.description: Dataset override (defaults come from the preset).

max_ops.description: Stop after this many measured operations (deterministic CI runs).

mix.description: Operation mix override (defaults come from the preset).

rate.description: Open-loop arrival rate in ops/s. Unset = closed loop (`knobs.concurrency` workers).

shape.description:
Time-varying open-loop rate: `ramp:FROM..TO/D`, `step:R1,R2,…/D` or
`diurnal[:MIN..MAX/PERIOD]` (makes the run open-loop; `rate` is then the diurnal peak).

verify.description: Verify CRC32C of whole-object reads and sampled writes.

description: One event of a running command (oprobe.events/9), as the app receives them

oneOf.description: First line of every stream.

One interval of the measurement window (as `report.timeline`: operations by their
start; failures, throttled responses, requests and retries when they happened). It is
sent once the interval after it has also closed; an operation still running then (a
retry chain longer than an interval) adds its requests, retries and failure to the
interval they happened in only when it ends, so `report.timeline` is the final count.

errors_count.description: Operations that failed in the interval.

ops_per_s.description: Operations started per second, failed ones included.

requests_count.description: Requests sent in the interval, retries included.

t_s.description: Start of the second, seconds from the window start.

throttled_count.description: Throttled responses received in the interval.

oneOf.description:
A finding (design v6 §3 "Explain"): a cause, the evidence (the requests themselves) and
**one** OpenDAL remedy. No sizing numbers: a single run varies no load (T1, T2); `oprobe
prove` sizes the remedy.

confidence.description:
How sure the cause is: `high` only when the limit model explains most of the effect
and agrees across the run's halves (T8).

oneOf.description: One trial run of a prove (an event as it finishes, and a row of the result).

backend_bytes.description:
Bytes the service sent and received in request and response bodies (9.4; absent in
earlier results): what a remedy costs in transfer, against `logical_bytes`.

error_ratio.description: Operations that failed for reasons other than throttling, per operation.

feasible.description:
Within `--max-throttle` and the error ratio a run allows (1 %), and, for the remedy of
a `rate_limit` finding, sending no more requests per second than the fitted limit.

logical_bytes.description: Bytes the application read and wrote (9.4; absent in earlier results).

p99_spread_ratio.description:
How far off this trial's p99 can be, as a log ratio: a quarter of the log width of the
latencies at the ranks 0.99·n ± 2·√(0.0099·n) of its n operations (the p99's
order-statistic interval). Above 0.17 those latencies differ by more than 2×: the p99
sits on a cliff. Absent when 0, and in results of 9.2 and earlier.

pair.description: The A/B pair (0-based) of a baseline or candidate trial.

run_id.description: The stored trial run (a child of the prove).

value.description: The sized value of a sizing trial (or the candidate's), as `--set` writes it.

oneOf.description: The command's result (last line of a successful stream).

data.description: The typed result of commands that do not produce a run.

path.description: Run file, when the command saved one.
